key_insight: Nonreciprocal spherical attention yields a sharp coarsening-time exponent of 1 − cos φ under stated assumptions, alongside certified corrections for compressed retrieval scores.
engineering_relevance: Mass-centered compression provides O(r²) attention-output error at fixed temperature, while calibrated scores can improve compressed nearest-neighbor rankings.
method: Prove coarsening clocks for shrinking spherical blocks and separated metastable exponents in a three-body flow.
Derive compression-error bounds with an explicit spherical-normalization correction.
Fit skew score corrections through a strictly convex moment problem, with residual certificates and bounded low-rank projections.
evidence_signal: On SIFT1M, skew calibration improves native-L2 hit@10 from 0.8926 to 0.8948 versus 0.8996 for symmetric calibration; a 10-million-vector index achieves 0.8827 hit@10 at 0.1794 ms/query in a four-thread batch benchmark.
watch_item: Directionality does not guarantee retrieval gains: validation selected no skew update for the 10-million-vector index.
paper_title: Nonreciprocal Spherical Attention and Retrieval: Sharp Coarsening Clocks and Certified Score Correction
